references.summary: Bulb crop usually propagated using cloves. Cold exposure influences development and bulbing; frost survival differs from a quantified injury threshold. Warm conditions and daylength interact with maturity and bulbing; storage injury is not standing-crop heat injury. Other Allium crops can share important soil-borne problems; garlic after garlic can maintain inoculum. Planting date, clove condition and cultivar determine the crop calendar; curing follows field harvest.
